[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility, Switch Las Vegas 8, is part of Switch Las Vegas Core Campus in Clark County, Nevada, spanning locations including Las Vegas, Enterprise, and near McCarran. Switch was founded in 2000 by Rob Roy, who serves as CEO and chief engineer, and the company is headquartered in Las Vegas. Wikipedia coverage states that in 2002 Roy acquired a former Enron facility in Las Vegas at auction for 930,000 dollars, strategically located over a fiber optic backbone serving technology companies nationwide, which became the foundation of the Las Vegas Core Campus. That campus has grown to eleven operating data centers spanning over 2 million square feet, with plans to reach 2.3 million square feet across 12 buildings. Switch also operates the Citadel Campus in Storey County in Northern Nevada, a separate 4 billion dollar, 1,000 plus acre development announced in January 2015, and a Grand Rapids, Michigan Pyramid Campus, but those are distinct from this Las Vegas registry cluster. In December 2022 DigitalBridge and IFM Investors completed an 11 billion dollar acquisition, taking Switch private. Data center industry directories place Switch Las Vegas 8 at 5225 W Capovilla Avenue, Las Vegas, NV. Sourced from datacenterHawk, a single aggregator directory, not independently corroborated by a second source this session.  Switch own official locations page (fetched directly this session, https://www.switch.com/locations/) names five exascale campuses, the Citadel in Tahoe Reno, the Pyramid Campus in Grand Rapids, the Core Campus in Las Vegas, the Keep Campus in Atlanta, and the Rock Campus in Austin and Houston, but confirms no street address for any campus or building, directing visitors to a contact form instead. reading.body:
Switch Las Vegas 8 is part of the Switch Las Vegas Core Campus, one of five exascale campuses the operator names publicly but for which the operator publishes no power specifications. The facility's power capacity is not published by Switch on its specification page. Nevada hosts 26 mapped data center facilities, only 2 of which have published power figures in this registry, totaling 10.37 MW of stated capacity across the state.

This campus ranks third in Nevada by published megawatts among the facilities this site has read, though that ranking reflects the sparsity of published specifications statewide rather than a definitive measure of the Las Vegas Core Campus's actual size. The operator acquired the foundation site in 2002 and has grown the Las Vegas campus to eleven operating buildings spanning over 2 million square feet, with plans to expand to 12 buildings and 2.3 million square feet. The campus is located over a fiber optic backbone serving technology companies nationwide, a topological advantage established two decades ago that persists.

Without published power specifications, this facility cannot be sized against the grid constraints that bind AI scaling. The absence of a stated figure, repeated across the operator's published locations despite the campus's scale and age, means this registry entry documents a location known to exist and to operate at significant physical footprint, but leaves its electric demand, and therefore its relevance to AI infrastructure capacity, unquantified.
